function.name: bash
function.description: Run a bash command in your Linux workspace container. The shell session PERSISTS across calls (cwd, env vars, background jobs); it resets if a command times out, floods output, or the workspace sat idle for ~10 minutes — files in /work always survive, so do not rely on env vars or cwd across long gaps. No network by default. User uploads are in /work/attachments/. Python 3 with Pillow and NumPy, ImageMagick, rsvg-convert for SVG, pdftotext, jq, file, and rg are installed. Use it to inspect uploaded files, compute geometry, analyze mc.dump exports, or generate data files for builds to read with mc.readFile.

command.description: The bash command to run. For python, always use a real multi-line heredoc: python3 - <<'EOF' (newline) code (newline) EOF — never cram code into python3 -c with \n escapes. Avoid interactive commands.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum run time in milliseconds (default 10000, max 120000).

network.description: Run this one command in a separate one-shot shell WITH internet access (persistent session state does not apply there; /work is shared). Use only when needed: pip install --target or venv under /work, downloading a reference. Default false. When downloading, use curl -fsSL (so HTTP errors fail loudly instead of saving an error page), verify with file/identify, and raise timeout_ms beyond the small default. Many sites (e.g. Wikimedia) block non-browser clients; raw.githubusercontent.com works reliably.
